Year 1 is anchored to the held FY2026 revenue guide (~$1.21B, +16.6%). Beyond FY2026 the base case runs at the ~9% bookings run-rate (Q2 2026 bookings +8%, Q3 guide +9%, FY +10-12%) with no re-acceleration: two consecutive quarters of widening DAU/bookings divergence and the Max-tier sunset removed the basis for one. The 5-year base revenue CAGR from FY2025 is 10.1%; a PEG reader should use that, not the 16.6% year-1 figure. EPS CAGRs excluded (FY2025 GAAP EPS $8.38 carries a $256.7M valuation-allowance release).

Revenue 3yr CAGR (41.1%) and FCF 3yr CAGR (70.4%) far exceed sustainable long-run growth. FY2026 guidance represents a significant deceleration: bookings growth slowing from 33% to 10-12%, Adj. EBITDA margins compressing ~370bps to ~25.7%. Selected growth rate anchored to guidance, not historical CAGRs.

notes.fcf_margin_note: FCF margin (34.7% of revenue in FY2025) is structurally higher than Adj EBITDA margin (29.5%) due to: (1) deferred revenue from annual subscriptions creating favorable working capital; (2) very low capex (~$27.4M in FY2025, 2.6% of revenue); (3) continued tax benefit utilization. notes.q3_2025_normalization: Q3 2025 net income of $292.2M includes approximately $256.7M in non-recurring deferred tax valuation-allowance release. This is a one-time accounting item with no cash impact and is excluded from all FCF-based projections, which are the correct basis for DUOL's valuation given the FCF >> GAAP net income dynamic from SBC and deferred revenue.
notes.sbc_adjusted_fcf: FCF CAGRs above are on REPORTED FCF. On the SBC-adjusted series the 3yr CAGR is not meaningful (FY2022 adjusted FCF was negative, -$0.5M), and the 2yr adjusted CAGR of 117.8% exceeds the reported 59.2% only because the FY2023 base is depressed by SBC — a low-base artifact, not accelerating growth. base.name: Base Case: Deceleration Sticks, Margins Recover
base.description: FY2026 lands on the held guidance (~$1.21B revenue, +16.6%; bookings +10-12%; adj. EBITDA ~26.5%). From FY2027 revenue growth converges to the ~9-11% bookings run-rate and stays there: the ~23% DAU / +17% subscriber growth is real volume, but the Max sunset (about 10% of the paid base at ~2x the Super price migrating onto Super pricing) and the Super Lite test dilute revenue per subscriber by roughly as much as volume adds. No re-acceleration is modelled. Adjusted EBITDA margin starts at the raised 26.5% guide and rebuilds to the FY2025 level (29.5%) by year 4 and 32% by year 9 as the structural AI-inference cost cut holds; the operating leverage is slower than the July path because revenue growth is lower.
base.reasoning: Y1 16.6%: H1 2026 actual revenue $590.5M plus the Q3 guide of ~$302M leaves Q4 at ~$317M (+12%) for the ~$1.21B held guide. Y2-Y3 9%: FY2027 revenue is recognised from bookings written in roughly H2 2026-H1 2027, which are guided at +9% (Q3) and +10-12% (FY); the Max ARPU compression is assumed to roughly offset subscriber volume. Y4-Y10 8,8,7,7,6,5,5: the same ~1pp/yr glide toward terminal growth the July file used, started from ~9% instead of from a re-accelerated ~14%. EBITDA 26.5% in Y1 is the raised guide; the path then rises ~1pp/yr to 30% by Y5 and 32% by Y9 (the July path reached the same 32% terminal margin; the first five years are ~1pp higher because the inference-cost cut is structural, the last five converge because growth is lower). SBC%, cash-tax ramp, D&A, capex, WC capture, WACC 10%, terminal growth 3% and the 20x cap are unchanged from July.

bull.name: Bull Case: DAU Base Monetizes With a Lag, Super Consolidation Widens the Funnel
bull.description: The DAU-to-bookings lag is a lag, not a break: the 58.7M-DAU base (up 23%) and record retention convert into bookings during FY2027-28, and folding Video Call/Roleplay into Super raises paid conversion enough to more than offset the Max ARPU give-up. Growth re-accelerates modestly in FY2028 (14%) rather than the 18-20% the July bull assumed, then glides. The ~97% AI-inference cost reduction plus scale takes adjusted EBITDA margin to 35% by year 9. Chess, Math and Music contribute at the margin.
bull.reasoning: Y1 17.5%: top half of the 15-18% guide (a Q4 beat). Y2 13%, Y3 14%, Y4 13%: the DAU base begins to monetize with a 12-18 month lag and Super consolidation lifts conversion; this is the bull axis and it is deliberately milder than the July bull (18/17/15). Y5-Y10 12,11,10,9,8,7 unchanged in shape. EBITDA path lifted ~0.5-1pp in Y1-Y4 for the AI cost cut, converging to the same 35% terminal margin. WACC 9%, terminal growth 3.5% carried forward.

bear.name: Bear Case: Monetization Never Converts, Max Sunset Compresses ARPU
bear.description: Two quarters of widening DAU/bookings divergence were the signal. The Max sunset removes ~8% of subscription revenue as former Max subscribers renew at Super prices, Super Lite trades down more of the base, and free AI assistants absorb casual conversational practice, so revenue is roughly flat in FY2027 (+2%) and grows ~3% thereafter. Margins hold around 26-27% only because the AI cost cut is structural; there is no operating leverage without growth. The company survives comfortably on its net cash but is ex-growth.
bear.reasoning: Y1 15.0%: low end of guidance (Q4 revenue +6%). Y2 2%: Max sunset ARPU hit (~8% of subscription revenue) lands on renewal with no volume offset, against bookings growth already in the high single digits and falling. Y3-Y7 3%, Y8-Y10 2%: ex-growth. EBITDA 26.0% in Y1 (Q4 shortfall against the 26.5% guide), 25.5% in Y2-Y3 as the ARPU cut hits a fixed cost base, then drifts to 27% by Y8 (the July bear's terminal margin) because the AI cost cut holds. SBC path is the July bear path (SBC does not fall with growth). WACC 11.5%, terminal growth 2% carried forward.

valuation_philosophy.framework: Component-built owner-FCF DCF, 10-year horizon, flat diluted share count
valuation_philosophy.rationale: Built on OWNER FREE CASH FLOW with margins constructed from components each year over ten years. FY2025 owner FCF = $360.4M reported - $148.6M SBC (company's adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation figure) - $45.2M interest income = $166.6M. That FY2025 margin is NOT carried forward: each year is adjusted EBITDA, less SBC (declining % of revenue), less D&A, taxed at a ramping cash rate, plus D&A, less capex, plus working capital on the CHANGE in revenue. (1) The deferred-revenue inflow was $123.3M in FY2025, 34% of reported FCF; it scales with bookings growth and shrinks as growth falls to ~9%, which is why the base year-1 owner-FCF margin is 12.4% and year-2 is 11.3%. (2) The FY2025 cash tax benefit is not repeatable; the rate ramps from -6% to 21% by year 5. (3) The horizon runs to year 10 because the base margin is still ramping at year 5 (13.2%) and only matures near 16.3% by year 10. SBC is charged exactly once, as an expense; the diluted count is held flat at 49.0M and the $72M of buybacks to date are value-neutral under that convention.
valuation_philosophy.what_changed_2026_09_21: The July base case carried a Y2-Y4 growth path of 12% -> 14% -> 13% (its prose said 20-22%), i.e. a re-acceleration reasoned on Max-tier adoption and DAU monetization. Q2 2026 delivered bookings +8% against DAU +23% (the gap widened from Q1's 14% vs 21%), FY bookings guidance was held at +10-12% despite a revenue beat, and in September 2026 Duolingo began sunsetting Max. The re-acceleration is retired: base growth now converges to the bookings run-rate (9%) and glides from there. The raised margin guidance (26.5% adj. EBITDA, >$375M FCF) from the ~97% AI-inference cost cut is credited as structural, lifting the first five years of the margin path by ~1pp; it is worth about +$1.3/share against roughly -$14/share for the growth change.
key_risks_to_framework: If FY2027 bookings growth re-accelerates into the teens as the DAU base monetizes, the base case is too low and the bull case (which needs only 13-14%) becomes the base.
If the Max sunset and Super Lite compress ARPU faster than volume offsets, FY2027 revenue growth could fall below the 9% base toward the 2% bear.
If SBC does not decline as a % of revenue (Q1 2026 ran 12.8% on the add-back basis), every scenario is overstated; SBC is the largest single swing factor.
If the AI-inference cost advantage proves transient (Q3 gross margin is guided back to ~71% from 72.6%), the +1pp margin lift reverses.
Per-scenario WACCs (9/10/11.5%) charge risk in the discount rate on top of the scenario weights; equalising at 10% is a pending house-rule clean-up.

key_assumptions_summary.why_guidance_based_growth: Duolingo's 2022-2025 hypergrowth (revenue CAGR 41%) is explicitly not the DCF base. FY2026 revenue is largely locked by H1 actuals ($590.5M) and the Q3 guide (~$302M). Beyond that the base case follows the bookings run-rate (+8% Q2, +9% Q3 guide, +10-12% FY) because revenue is recognised from bookings with a ~5-month lag and the Max sunset removes the ARPU lever the July re-acceleration relied on.
key_assumptions_summary.growth_path_change: Base Y2-Y4 was 12/14/13 (July, a re-acceleration); now 9/9/8. Bull Y2-Y4 was 18/17/15; now 13/14/13. Bear Y2-Y5 was 8/7/6/5; now 2/3/3/3. The late-year glides were lowered to start from the new levels rather than from a re-accelerated one.
key_assumptions_summary.margin_path_change: FY2026 adj. EBITDA guide raised to ~26.5% (from ~25.7% at Q1 and ~25% in February) on a ~97% reduction in Video Call inference cost ($0.30 -> <$0.01/call) after moving off GPT-4. Credited as structural: base Y1 25.5% -> 26.5%, Y2-Y5 +1pp; terminal 32% unchanged because slower growth means less operating leverage. Q2 gross margin 72.6% vs the ~69% Q4 trough previously guided.
key_assumptions_summary.max_tier_sunset: As of September 2026 new subscribers cannot choose Max; its AI features are in Super. ~10% of the paid base at ~2x the Super price implies Max was ~18% of subscription revenue; migrating those subscribers to Super pricing is a ~8-9% subscription-revenue headwind spread over renewal cycles. Base assumes volume (subs +17%, DAU +23%) roughly offsets it; bull assumes conversion gains exceed it; bear assumes no offset.
key_assumptions_summary.net_cash_position: Net cash $1,251.6M = $1,138.6M cash and equivalents + $113.0M short-term Treasuries, zero debt, at 2026-03-31 (Q1 2026 10-Q) -- $25.54 per diluted share. The Treasuries were omitted from the July anchor although their interest was stripped from FCF. Q2 2026 FCF of $79M less ~$44M buybacks implies ~$1.28B by June 30, not used as an anchor because the Q2 balance sheet is not in Metrics.csv.
key_assumptions_summary.terminal_growth_justification: 3% base (long-run nominal GDP), 3.5% bull, 2% bear, all carried forward. Gordon binds in every scenario (implied exit multiples 14.7x / 18.8x / 10.7x owner FCF, all below the 20x cap).
key_assumptions_summary.wacc_justification: 10% base carried forward: risk-free ~4.3%, ERP ~5%, beta ~1.05, zero debt so WACC = cost of equity. Bull 9% and bear 11.5% inherited from July; flagged as a risk-charged-twice deviation to be equalised in a future pass.
key_assumptions_summary.eps_normalization: FY2025 GAAP net income $414.1M includes a $256.7M deferred-tax valuation-allowance release; normalized ~$157.4M. Q2 2026 GAAP net income $33.2M (11.1% margin) vs $44.8M a year earlier reflects the tax rate normalising, not a cash deterioration.

investment_recommendation.summary: On fully SBC-expensed owner FCF, DUOL at $141.90 trades 33% above the base IV of $95.67 and 27% above the weighted $102.96. Only the bull case ($170.10) clears the price, and it requires the DAU-to-bookings lag to close in FY2027-28 after two quarters in which it widened. The headline IV is higher than July's $87.97 solely because the July file double-charged dilution; on like-for-like conventions the Q2 print and the Max sunset took roughly 10% off the value, and the raised margin guide gave back about one-tenth of that. Net cash of $25.54/share bounds the downside; the 15% hurdle entry price is $64.03 weighted ($63.26 base).
investment_recommendation.bull_thesis: DAU +23% and record retention are real; if bookings follow with a 12-18 month lag and folding Video Call/Roleplay into Super lifts conversion, FY2027-28 growth re-accelerates to 13-14% and the ~97% inference-cost cut lets margins reach 35% -- worth ~$170/share. The $400M buyback (18% deployed) and $1.25B net cash mean the balance sheet is not a constraint.
key_risks: Bookings/DAU divergence widened for a second quarter (Q2: +8% vs +23%); FY26 bookings guide held at +10-12% despite the revenue beat, Q3 guided +9%.
Max sunset (September 2026): ~10% of paid base at ~2x Super price migrates down; Super Lite tests a lower price point again.
AI substitution: the same open-source models that cut Duolingo's inference cost 97% cut the barrier for free conversational-practice competitors.
SBC ~15% of revenue with revenue growth now ~9%: the SBC charge falls as a share of revenue only if management holds dollars roughly flat.
Stock rallied 14-22% into mid-September on narrative and upgrades without a bookings change; Q3 (early November) is the next hard test.
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 print (early November): bookings vs the ~$307M / +9% guide, first read on Max-to-Super migration and Super Lite.
FY2027 guidance (February 2027): whether bookings growth is guided back into double digits.
Buyback pace: $72M of $400M through Q2; acceleration at ~$140 would signal management sees value below the street basis.
Gross margin holding ~71-72% through Q4 would confirm the inference-cost cut is structural.
investment_recommendation.margin_of_safety: None at $141.90 on the house basis: the price is above the base and weighted IVs and 74% of the way to the street value. 25 of 25 sensitivity cells sit below the price. Entry at the 15% hurdle requires $64.03 weighted.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
